systems.finding: Aesop closes project-level S5 structurally through authoritative project-root AGENTS.md policy that can be synthesized through supported /init and edited by the legitimate parent, then loaded into later project operation. A public upstream LANE-CONTRACT.md development-history chain was inspected but belongs to development of the Aesop repository itself rather than a target-project operating cell, so using it as a canonical Aesop capability result would cross the declared recursion/boundary. No target-project policy-change-to-subsequent-operation result is admitted.
reassess_if: a public target-project Aesop run records an identity/ultimate-policy issue, the /init or legitimate parent decision, the resulting authoritative AGENTS.md change and later project-agent operation under that exact changed policy
a benchmark or case study publishes immutable before/after evidence for the same supported project-policy path

systems.finding: Bernstein closes parent-owned S5 structurally through a content-addressed governance playbook protocol in which a model may draft but a human signs the exact policy before govern apply can enact it. Public source and tests establish the authority/enforcement mechanism, but the reviewed repository did not expose a committed real signed govern-plan/lineage artifact together with a later Bernstein run consuming that enacted policy. Test-only temporary signed instances are not promoted to a capability observation.
reassess_if: Bernstein publishes an immutable signed governance playbook plus provenance showing govern apply and a subsequent run governed by that exact signed state
a first-party case study or benchmark measures policy enactment and later operation through the shipped governance path

systems.finding: DotCraft closes parent-owned S5 structurally through durable Agent Profiles: a legitimate author selects role and capability policy, the runtime compiles the selected profile into a persisted thread configuration with profile provenance/fingerprint, and conversations or unattended work can execute under that snapshot. Public implementation, documentation, SDK samples and tests establish the mechanism, but no immutable real profile-policy change linked to a subsequent production-like thread/Goal/Automation result was recovered, so no direct S5 observation is admitted.
reassess_if: DotCraft publishes a committed concrete Agent Profile plus an immutable subsequent thread/Goal/Automation artifact carrying that exact profile id/fingerprint
a benchmark compares governed operation before and after an authoritative Agent Profile policy change

systems.finding: HugAgentOS closes S5 structurally at project recursion through authoritative project-root AGENTS.md policy: supported /init can synthesize and persist rules, legitimate project editors/admins can edit them, and later project conversations receive the changed policy. Targeted public-result search did not recover a reusable benchmark or immutable enacted-policy run binding a concrete rule change to subsequent measured operation, so this remains canonical mechanism evidence rather than a direct S5 capability observation.
reassess_if: HugAgentOS publishes an immutable /init or editor-authored AGENTS.md change and a later project run demonstrably governed by that exact changed policy
a first-party experiment measures project-policy construction or amendment quality and subsequent operation

reassess_if: Octos publishes a concrete IDENTITY.md/SOUL.md change with immutable provenance and a later run showing the changed bootstrap state governing operation
a first-party benchmark or case study measures identity/policy amendment through the shipped hot-reload path

non_claim: This delta does not claim absence of all possible S5 evidence in the public ecosystem. It records that the newly S5-positive canonical systems admitted after the frozen cohort materially expand mechanism/ownership coverage, while this review did not recover a new reusable direct canonical S5 capability observation satisfying the existing primary-reopen criteria.
